definition.def: If you assign a piece of work to someone, you give them the work to do.
examples: When I taught, I would assign a topic to children which they would write about. [VERB noun + to]
Later in the year, she'll assign them research papers. [VERB noun noun]
When teachers assign homework, students usually feel an obligation to do it. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you assign something to someone, you say that it is for their use.
examples: The selling broker is then required to assign a portion of the commission to the buyer broker. [VERB noun + to]
He assigned her all his land in Ireland. [VERB noun noun]

definition.def: If someone is assigned to a particular place, group, or person, they are sent there, usually in order to work at that place or for that person.
examples: I was assigned to Troop A of the 10th Cavalry. [be VERB-ed + to]
Did you choose Russia or were you simply assigned there? [be V-ed adv]
Each of us was assigned a minder, someone who looked after us. [be VERB-ed noun]

definition.def: If you assign a particular function or value to someone or something, you say they have it.
examples: Under Mr. Harel's system, each business must assign a value to each job. [VERB noun + to]
Assign the letters of the alphabet their numerical values–A equals 1, B equals 2, etc. [VERB noun noun]
